title: Taylor Series Convergence for Sin and Cos

problemStatement.formal: \text{Taylor partial sums } S_n(x) \to \sin(x) \text{ and } \cos(x) \text{ for all } x \in \mathbb{R}
problemStatement.plain: Prove that the Taylor series of sin and cos converge to sin(x) and cos(x) for all real x, using the period-4 property of their derivatives and the fact that all derivatives are bounded by 1.
whyMatters: Extends the exp Taylor convergence to all fundamental entire functions

knownResults.goal: Complete formalization of sin/cos Taylor convergence

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: TaylorSinCosConvergence.lean - 348 lines, 31 theorems, 2 axioms, 0 sorries. Period-4 derivative cycle, universal norm bound, convergence, summability, tighter-than-exp comparison.
insights: Period-4 proved by induction: base case iteratedDeriv 4 f = f, successor case uses iteratedDeriv_succ + ih
Norm bound reduces to 4 base cases via n mod 4 reduction using period-4
Sin/cos remainder |x|^{n+1}/n! is tighter than exp remainder exp(|x|)|x|^{n+1}/n! since |derivatives| ≤ 1
Summability of sinSeries/cosSeries via comp_injective subseries comparison with summable_pow_div_factorial
